name: WAINER APTER
description: Concurred, argued that constitutional ex post facto prohibitions only forbid punishment beyond what was contemplated at the time the crime was committed, and since the law at the time of Krug's offenses permitted the Board to consider all existing information, the 1997 amendment created no risk of additional punishment.

name: JUSTICE NORIEGA
description: Dissented, argued that the State should not retroactively apply a parole law that poses a greater risk of prolonged incarceration, as the 1979 Act established a social compact with incarcerated individuals, and the 1997 amendment retroactively imposed harsher conditions, violating ex post facto principles of notice and governmental restraint.

name: PATTERSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Daniel's Law is narrowly tailored to protect public officials from harm and reprisal, upholding the law against a journalist's free speech challenge.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE RABNER
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: JUSTICES FASCIALE
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: HOFFMAN
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: RABNER, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that it was premature for the trial court to conclude that any potential presentment had to be suppressed, as no grand jury had completed an investigation or issued a presentment.

name: GILSON, P.J.A.D.
description: Concurred, argued that N.J.S.A. 19:13-8 is constitutional under the Anderson-Burdick interest-balancing test, as it imposes only a minimal burden on rights and serves the state's compelling regulatory interests in election integrity and political stability.

name: FASCIALE, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the charity care program is not an unconstitutional taking because it does not physically appropriate property or constitute a regulatory taking, given the highly regulated nature of the hospital industry and the paramount public interest it serves.

name: RABNER, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the State Constitution guarantees an affirmative right to speak freely, and the regulation, despite its legitimate aims, reaches too far and chills constitutionally protected speech, making it overbroad.

name: JUSTICE WAINER APTER
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: WAINER APTER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the witness tampering statute is not facially overbroad but may have been unconstitutionally applied to the defendant, requiring a new trial with proper jury instructions on intent.

name: WAINER APTER
description: Concurred, argued that a mens rea of recklessness is constitutionally sufficient for true threats, but an objective component (reasonable person similarly situated to the victim) is also necessary, and juries must unanimously agree on the specific subsection violated.

name: JUSTICE PIERRE-LOUIS
description: Concurred, arguing that a generalized smell of raw marijuana does not justify a search of every compartment of an automobile, and the search of the engine compartment and trunk exceeded the scope of the automobile exception.

name: RABNER, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that first-time in-court identifications are inherently suggestive and risk depriving defendants of due process rights, and that continuous narration of video evidence by an investigator who did not witness the event is improper.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE RABNER
description: Concurred, argued that law enforcement must adhere to the heightened protections of the New Jersey Wiretap Act for prospective electronic communications, as a CDW based on probable cause is insufficient to protect individual privacy.

name: JUSTICE FASCIALE
description: Concurred, argued that the police actions leading to the warrantless search were deliberate and orchestrated, not unforeseeable and spontaneous, thus requiring a warrant under the New Jersey Constitution's automobile exception.

name: FASCIALE, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that a new heightened discovery standard is necessary to balance a sexual assault victim's confidential communications with a defendant's right to a meaningful defense.

name: JUSTICE ALBIN
description: Concurred, argued that the attorney-review requirement of N.J.S.A. 25:1-5(h) for palimony agreements violates the substantive due process guarantee of the New Jersey Constitution by interfering with individual autonomy and the right to contract without compelled legal counsel.

name: JUSTICE FERNANDEZ-VINA
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: JUSTICE PIERRE-LOUIS
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE RABNER
description: Concurred, arguing that the statutory framework for sentencing juveniles, without a review mechanism, contravenes the State Constitution, and a 20-year look-back period is necessary to save the statute from constitutional infirmity.

name: JUSTICE SOLOMON
description: Dissented, arguing that the majority's imposition of a 20-year lookback period for juvenile offenders was a subjective policy decision that overstepped the judiciary's role and should be left to the Legislature.

name: JUSTICE PIERRE-LOUIS
description: Concurred, argued that fundamental fairness prohibits courts from subjecting a defendant to enhanced sentencing for conduct a jury found the defendant not guilty of, thereby protecting the integrity of the jury trial right.

name: JUSTICE ALBIN
description: Concurred, argued that arrestees have a reasonable expectation of privacy in police station phone calls without notice of recording, and such warrantless, non-consensual recordings violate constitutional privacy protections.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE RABNER
description: Concurred, argued that the statute should be interpreted narrowly to require legibility and identifiability of license plate markings, and that the 'reasonable mistake of law' doctrine should not be adopted under the New Jersey Constitution to protect individual rights against unreasonable searches and seizures.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE RABNER
description: Concurred, argued that the defendant's constitutional right to a fair trial was violated due to implicit or unconscious racial bias in the jury selection process, and established new rules for criminal history checks on prospective jurors.

name: JUSTICE ALBIN
description: Concurred, argued that the virtual grand jury format, as a temporary measure during a public health crisis, preserves the constitutional right to a grand jury presentation without sacrificing core principles, and the Court has the authority to implement such procedures.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE RABNER
description: Concurred, argued that the Criminal Justice Reform Act (CJRA) does not authorize judges to detain non-citizens based on potential removal by immigration officials, as detention should be based on a defendant's own volitional acts.

name: JUSTICE ALBIN
description: Other, dissented in Lopez-Carrera arguing that the majority's decision strips the State of its sovereign power to prosecute foreign nationals and denies crime victims their rights by preventing detention of non-citizens facing certain and imminent removal by ICE, but concurred in Molchor and Rios as their removals were not certain and imminent.

name: JUSTICE PIERRE-LOUIS
description: Other, concurred with Justice Albin's opinion.

name: JUSTICE PATTERSON
description: Concurred, delivered the opinion of the Court, arguing that release time provisions are authorized by statute and do not violate the Gift Clause, serving a public purpose by promoting labor peace and efficient school management.
